raw.description: Hardcoded secret in environment variable configuration.
raw.exploit: If an attacker gains access to the environment configuration, they can use the JWT secret to forge tokens.

raw.description: JWT token is set with 'secure: true', which is good, but if the application is accessed over HTTP, it could be exposed.
raw.exploit: If the application is accessed over HTTP instead of HTTPS, the token could be intercepted by an attacker.

raw.description: CSRF protection is implemented using 'csurf', but the configuration might not be sufficient if the application is not using HTTPS.
raw.exploit: An attacker could potentially perform CSRF attacks if the application is accessed over HTTP.

raw.description: Error messages reveal internal server errors which can be used for information gathering.
raw.exploit: An attacker can use the error messages to gain insights into the server's structure and potential vulnerabilities.

raw.description: Sensitive data (username and password) is sent over the network without explicit HTTPS enforcement.
raw.exploit: An attacker could intercept the login credentials if the application is accessed over an insecure connection.

raw.description: Lack of proper access control on file download endpoint.
raw.exploit: An authenticated user could attempt to download files they do not own by manipulating the file ID in the URL.
